title: Code Task policy af.code-task-policy/1
description: The captured form of a repository's `.af/code-policy.toml`: the named checks a code Task runs against a read-only Snapshot and, optionally, the Warm Check Cache those checks may use (ADR-0131). A policy without `warm` is captured exactly as before the table existed. Optional `measures` and `objectives` declare the commands the installed `measure` operator runs and the objectives `compare` folds two Measurements under (ADR-0132); a policy without them is captured exactly as before the tables existed. A check's optional `remote` table declares the same check run by a remote executor (ADR-0140); only an operator's machine-local mapping selects it, and a policy without it is captured exactly as before the table existed.

check_wall_ms.description: The whole check Attempt's wall. Without check_process_wall_ms, at most 5400000 (90 minutes). With an explicit per-process cap, at most max(3600000, check_process_wall_ms times the number of checks); the typed validator checks that cross-field bound.

rust_toolchain.description: Optional named native checks whose Rust tools come from the operator's explicit machine mapping (ADR-0127): the exact release, the host (`native` or a triple), the components and the checks that use it. Refused together with require_container = true.

offline.description: The check runs without network (ADR-0207): npm reads only its cache, the warm layer's `npm_cache`, and every proxy variable names a closed local port. Needs [warm] build_cache to declare npm_cache.

npm_packages.description: The npm packages an offline check runs, each an exact `name@version` pinned by the SHA-256 of its registry tarball. The kernel fills the npm cache once, with the network, when a pin is absent, and verifies every pin before each run; only an offline check pins packages.

warm.description: An explicitly unsafe, machine-local layer only a trusted_local check touches: toolchain-keyed, byte-bounded build directories (`cargo_target` bound as CARGO_TARGET_DIR, `cargo_home` bound as CARGO_HOME, `npm_cache` bound as npm_config_cache) and administrator-approved Cache Snapshots. A declared `cargo` Cache Snapshot supersedes a `cargo_home` directory. Refused together with require_container = true. A check waits for a layer another check holds until its deadline, or builds in a private copy with `clone_when_busy`; its build phase has its own deadline, `build_wall_ms` (ADR-0207).

max_bytes.description: The eviction bound shared by every build directory of one toolchain key; 8 GiB when absent. A key above it is removed before a check and after one, whose result stands (ADR-0135).

hard_max_bytes.description: The only bound that ends a running check, with `warm_cache_bound_exceeded` (ADR-0135): twice `max_bytes` when absent, at most 32 GiB. It may not be below `max_bytes`, which the typed policy checks.

clone_when_busy.description: When another check holds the layer, build in a private copy of it (clonefile on APFS, a reflink on btrfs and XFS, else a plain copy) instead of waiting for it (ADR-0207). Absent or false, a check waits until its deadline.

build_wall_ms.description: The deadline of a check's build phase, from its start until it reports its `build` step through `$AF_CHECK_REPORT`; check_wall_ms then governs its tests. 2400000 when absent. A check Attempt under [warm] has check_wall_ms plus build_wall_ms (ADR-0207).

measure.description: A measured command: repeated `repetitions` times, each bounded by `wall_ms`, against a read-only Snapshot. `warm = true` binds the Warm Check Cache's cargo_target directory as CARGO_TARGET_DIR and needs [warm] build_cache to declare it; `false` binds a fresh directory in the repetition's runtime directory. `elapsed_ms` is always recorded; `metrics` are what the command reports.

objective.description: What a comparison concludes against: one measure, one of its metrics, the better direction, the minimum improvement ratio (0 to 1; a strictly positive improvement is always required) and the minimum repetitions on each side (default 3).

remote.description: The same check run by a remote executor (ADR-0140). `executor` is a closed set; `workflow` is the repository path of the workflow whose `pull_request` run earns the result; `required` lists the job names, exactly as the Actions jobs API reports them for that run, that must all conclude `success`. Committed policy never forces a remote run: an operator's machine-local mapping selects it, and the check's `command` stays its local equivalent.
